reason: The text extensively emphasizes hierarchical authority structures throughout the narrative. Kings exercise supreme authority (melech appears repeatedly); subordinate officials execute their rulers' commands; clear chains of authority are depicted (Sennacherib commanding his Rabshakeh and officers; Hezekiah directing his officials); and formal protocols of hierarchical communication are observed (messages between kings, officials meeting with kings). The entire structure of the narrative reinforces authority flowing from God down through kings to subjects and common people. The text presents hierarchy as the natural, accepted order of both Assyrian and Judahite governance without questioning its legitimacy.
